sequence.folder_help: Add videos and images in a folder as separate jobs. To turn consecutive images into one video, use Add image sequence.

sequence.help: Find consecutive numbered images with the same prefix, suffix and extension in this folder, sorted numerically. Supports same-size SDR PNG/JPG and HDR PNG; originals are not modified.

guidance.nvofa_hint: RAFT-Large is a neural network model; NVOFA uses NVIDIA hardware optical flow without model weights or iterations. Both support the direction handling below. NVOFA initialization failure is reported before trying RAFT. Runtime failure stops processing; no mid-video switch.
guidance.grid_hint: One motion vector per block. 4×4 works on every Optical Flow NVIDIA GPU; 2×2 and 1×1 need Ampere or newer and are denser, usually slower. Turing is 4×4 only.
guidance.error.flow_grid_component: This component does not provide the selected output grid. 4×4 works; 2×2 / 1×1 need an updated NVOFA component.

guidance.error.nvofa_cuda: NVOFA requires an NVIDIA GPU. Select Auto/CUDA, or choose RAFT.
guidance.error.nvofa_mixed: NVOFA currently supports flow-only mode. Use RAFT for maintainer mixed-depth mode.
guidance.error.nvofa: NVOFA failed. Check GPU/driver and retry, or choose RAFT.
guidance.flow_page_hint: Estimate frame motion for enhancement and flow export. Depth inference is temporarily unavailable in this release.
guidance.edge_hint: Analysis long-edge limit, not export size. Flow supports up to 2048; values above 1280 are experimental and require an updated component, with substantially higher RAFT memory/time costs. Defaults are unchanged; resizing cannot add source detail.
guidance.export.hint: Export only the depth/flow visualization at source size and frame rate, without audio, the original image or UI overlays. PNG is an 8-bit visualization, not raw floating-point data.

guidance.legend.flow: Vectors: red = right, yellow-green = down, cyan = left, purple = up. Default backward flow maps current to previous frame. Adjust range in Map display (analysis-canvas px/frame). Inference-paced playback; no audio.

message.dlss_platform_error:
NGX returned 0xBAD00002 (PlatformError): an underlying graphics platform or system dependency failed. This does not mean the GPU is unsupported or prove that VRAM is exhausted. If CreateFeature failed, image processing has not started.

Save a full report via About → Export diagnostics. Check the actual DLL path, version/SHA256, NVIDIA driver, and separate v2/legacy logs. Use a fully extracted trusted package. Basic enhancement in the lite package does not require the optical-flow add-on; do not install models or blindly replace DLLs for this error.

tooltip.settings:
A disabled slider is processed as 0; enabling it restores the remembered value.
A skin-mask value of 0 is equivalent to off; values above 0 enable automatic masking.
tooltip.clear_media: Unload the current video or image and release decoder, audio, and DLSS host resources.
tooltip.add_queue: Add the current video or image to the export queue with the current processing and export settings.
tooltip.cancel_export: Stop the current video export and remove its incomplete output file.
tooltip.preview_performance:
Playback quality affects real-time playback only. Pausing, frame stepping, and releasing the scrubber still render an exact full-resolution frame.
A larger cache window uses more memory.
tooltip.export_settings: Set output resolution, encoding quality or target bitrate, and export performance. Parallel mode preserves visual quality but does not guarantee pixel-identical temporal results.
tooltip.advanced_host: The backend switches in an isolated process without restarting the UI. These options are locked during export to preserve sequencing.
tooltip.timeline: Light cyan: rendered with current settings; gray-cyan: decoded and waiting to render.
tooltip.play: Play / pause (Space). Playback stops on the final frame.
tooltip.audio: Play source audio during preview. Click to mute or unmute.
tooltip.views: 1 Original  ·  2 Enhanced  ·  3 Compare. Wheel to zoom; right-drag to pan when zoomed (left-drag panning is also retained). Left-drag the divider, or Shift+left-drag anywhere to move it. Hold Alt for the original.
tooltip.detach: Preview in a freely resizable separate window
tooltip.dock: Dock the preview back into the main window
tooltip.fullscreen: Fullscreen preview (F11 or double-click; Esc to exit)
tooltip.queue_output: Affects newly added jobs only. Choose Source folder to export beside each source. To update existing jobs, select them, right-click and choose Change selected output folder.
tooltip.apply_settings: Apply the current processing and export settings to selected jobs, keeping each job's output folder
tooltip.pause_queue: Pause the queue after the current job
tooltip.cancel_queue: Cancel the current job, pause the queue, and remove its incomplete file
tooltip.strength: Adjust NR strength for this pass, separately from output mix and overall enhancement. Off remembers the value and uses 0; on restores it.
tooltip.local_tone: Adjust this pass's influence on image tones. Off remembers the value and uses 0; on restores it.
tooltip.local_structure: Adjust this pass's influence on image structure. Off remembers the value and uses 0; on restores it.
tooltip.skin_mask: Skin structure is processed as 0 when disabled. When enabled above 0, automatic masking protects skin texture; 0 is equivalent to off.
tooltip.experimental_range: Normal range: 0–1.00. Enable to adjust strength, local tone, local structure, skin mask and output mix up to 5.00. Set values back within 1.00 before disabling; values are never silently clamped. Above 1.00 may cause clipping, artifacts or over-processing, not a quality percentage.
tooltip.playback_quality: Auto mode processes 4K-class media at 1080p during real-time playback and restores full resolution when paused.
tooltip.render_after_scrub: After scrubbing or seeking stops, wait this long before rendering the current frame's exact preview. Subsequent frames are rendered only when automatic pre-render is enabled.
tooltip.auto_prerender: When enabled, render subsequent frames while paused for smoother playback. Off by default: update only the current frame to reduce background GPU use; playback still buffers as needed. Your choice is saved automatically.
tooltip.preset: Slower presets are generally more compression-efficient; this is separate from image quality and target bitrate.
tooltip.container: Video can be exported as MP4, MKV, or MOV. Match input supports those three containers; M4V is treated as MP4, while AVI and WebM safely fall back to MP4. Images keep their source format.
tooltip.hdr_precision: PQ/HLG input uses RGBA16F for Feature 18 and exports as HEVC Main10. When disabled, input is tone-mapped to SDR; SDR output uses HEVC if either dimension exceeds 4096, otherwise H.264.
tooltip.output_mix:
Applies only to Processed. 0 is the original and 1 is full DLSS; values above 1 amplify the processed residual. DLSS/Compare preview and export use the same setting.
When disabled, the mix is 0 (original); enabling restores the remembered mix.
tooltip.output_view:
The export view affects export composition only; the preview above always uses Processed composition.
Processed blends DLSS with the original using Output mix.
Difference ×10 exports the amplified difference; gray means little change.
Side by side places the original on the left and DLSS on the right with a white divider.
tooltip.rate_control: Quality based keeps compression quality stable while file size varies. Target bitrate makes size easier to control, but complex scenes may fluctuate.
tooltip.resolution: Controls video output dimensions while preserving aspect ratio and never enlarging lower-resolution media. DLSS still processes at source resolution, so downscaling output does not reduce neural-rendering time.
tooltip.slider_input: Drag or enter a value directly; percentages such as 75% are supported.
tooltip.slider_range: The default maximum is 1.00 (100%). Enable the experimental 5× range for a maximum of 5.00 (500%).
tooltip.super_resolution: RTX Video Super Resolution enlarges the image first, then DLSS 5 runs at the target resolution. SDR and 10-bit HDR are supported; high resolutions significantly increase VRAM, RAM, and processing time.
hint.cache_estimate: About {frames} frames ({seconds:.1f} s) at {width}×{height}. Original, DLSS and guidance share this budget and reclaim it automatically.

message.dlss_runtime_unsupported:
NVIDIA NGX returned 0xBAD00001 (FeatureNotSupported), so the current GPU, driver, and runtime combination is unsupported. This happens before image processing and is normally unrelated to the image dimensions or format.

First make sure the application uses the NVIDIA discrete GPU:
1. Open Windows Settings → System → Display → Graphics.
2. Add or select DLSS5Tool.exe, then choose Options.
3. Select High performance (NVIDIA GPU) and save.
4. Fully exit and restart DLSS5Tool; avoid running it through Remote Desktop when possible.

Then verify that nvngx_dlssnr.dll matches the GPU generation:
RTX 30 series: download 30系.zip from Releases
RTX 40 series: use the default runtime included with the main application
RTX 50 series: download 50系.zip from Releases

Close the application and place the replacement in mods\nvngx_dlssnr.dll and select it in Runtime & model paths; the old _internal\nvngx_dlssnr.dll does not need to be overwritten. If it still fails, update the NVIDIA driver and use About → Export diagnostics to generate a log for the maintainer.

Releases: {releases_url}
guidance.iterations_hint: Updates per frame pair. Default: 6. More is slower, not always more accurate.
guidance.direction_hint: Supported by both RAFT and NVOFA. Recommended: estimate directly from current to previous frame. Negated forward (formerly Fork method) estimates previous-to-current flow, then negates vectors without remapping their positions. Errors may occur at motion boundaries and occlusions. For legacy comparison only, not a quality tier.
guidance.depth_hint: Models need matching weights. Higher stability slows range changes; it smooths normalization bounds, not contours. Default: 0.9.
guidance.percentile_hint: Default: P1–P99. Limits extreme values during normalization; not metric distance or clipping planes.
guidance.display_hint: Affects map preview and export only, not predictions or enhanced video. Lower range reveals small motion; units are analysis-canvas pixels/frame.
guidance.direction_legend: Vectors: red = right, yellow-green = down, cyan = left, purple = up. Default backward flow is not forward playback motion.

guidance.error.parameters_component: Component did not confirm analysis parameters. Update the complete add-on, or restore both original edges, 6 iterations, stability 0.9 and P1–P99.

realtime.effects.description.nr: DLSS NR enhances detail and structure at the current resolution. It is the default effect and requires a compatible NR runtime; it does not raise the game's engine frame rate.
realtime.effects.description.dlss: DLSS SR upscales captured frames. Set output scaling and provide a compatible runtime. Capture lacks native game depth and motion vectors, so this is not equivalent to in-game DLSS.
realtime.effects.description.fg: DLSS FG generates intermediate frames for smoother presentation. It does not raise game simulation FPS or guarantee lower input latency. Use only one frame-generation effect per chain.
realtime.effects.description.rate: Frame-rate filtering controls the cadence entering later processing. It does not generate frames or new detail.
realtime.effects.description.downscale: SSimDownscaler reduces image size rather than enlarging it. Use with the output scaling settings.
realtime.effects.description.scale: Scaling changes image dimensions. Bilinear, bicubic, Lanczos and neural variants differ in sharpness and cost. Start with one main scaling algorithm and compare the result.
realtime.effects.description.anime: Animation and line-art families such as Anime4K and CuNNy include different models, scales and quality variants. Try them on animation; compare carefully on realistic games. Complex variants generally cost more.
realtime.effects.description.pixel: Pixel-art scaling preserves or reconstructs block-like edges in pixel games and artwork. It is not a default choice for every realistic scene.
realtime.effects.description.sharpen: Sharpening increases edge contrast; it does not necessarily restore true detail. Excessive strength or repeated passes can introduce halos and noise.
realtime.effects.description.antialias: Post-process anti-aliasing smooths existing jagged edges, sometimes at the cost of sharpness. It cannot replace temporal data from the game engine.
realtime.effects.description.color: Color and gradient processing adjusts colors or brightness, or reduces banding. See the parameters for this effect; this is not upscaling or frame generation.
realtime.effects.description.crt: CRT effects simulate scanlines, display masks and a retro appearance. They are stylistic, not required image-repair steps.
realtime.effects.description.frames: Frame effects handle generation or pacing. Check the effect name and parameters; generated frames are different from real game frames.
realtime.effects.description.diagnostic: Diagnostic effects help inspect the processing chain. They are normally unnecessary during play.
realtime.effects.description.utility: Diagnostic utilities inspect the chain rather than providing a required enhancement step.
realtime.effects.description.enhance: Same-resolution enhancement adjusts detail in the current frame. Output size is still controlled by scaling settings.
realtime.effects.description.other: Third-party or uncategorized effect: original names and all parameters are preserved. Read its parameters and compare it separately before adding it to a regular chain.

export.preflight.title: Export resource advice
export.preflight.ram_peak: Available system memory is below the processing estimate. Reduce the cache budget, close other tasks, or reduce the output size. Splitting the duration alone does not reduce per-frame memory requirements.
export.preflight.vram_peak: Available video memory is below the processing estimate. Reduce the upscale factor or output size, or close other GPU tasks. Splitting the duration alone does not reduce per-frame video memory requirements.
export.preflight.vram_margin: Video memory headroom is tight. Models and drivers may allocate additional resources; try a short clip with the same settings first.
export.preflight.large_output: Processing above 4K may substantially increase full-frame transfers, processing time and resource peaks. Try a short clip with the same settings first.
export.preflight.long_run: This is a long upscaling task. Long-run memory stability has not been confirmed in this environment; duration alone does not imply video memory exhaustion.
export.preflight.unknown_resources: System or video memory headroom could not be fully queried, so resource risk cannot be assessed reliably.
export.preflight.long_advice: Test a short clip from the same source and observe speed and memory before deciding whether to split and process it sequentially. The cache budget is not a process-wide memory limit; the whole video need not be cached. Segment boundaries may differ visually. Automatic segmentation and resume are not available.
export.preflight.continue: This advice does not guarantee success or failure. Continue exporting?
tooltip.decode_cpu_fallback: Off by default. If GPU decoding cannot start, allow CPU decoding; enhancement and upscaling still use the GPU. CPU decoding may be slower. With this disabled, unsupported input prompts you to transcode first. Running jobs keep their starting settings.
